es.meaning: To be worth it; worth the effort.
es.regionNote: Peninsular Spanish also says 'merecer la pena'.

it.meaning: To be worth it; worth the effort.

bridge.note: A near-perfect cognate pair — same verb, same 'pena' — with one small Italian word doing all the damage: ne. Italian says NE vale la pena ('it's worth it [of it]'), and that partitive has no Spanish counterpart to map from. The same ne that carries averne fin sopra i capelli, earning its keep again.

interference.es_to_it: Spanish speakers say 'vale la pena' in Italian — understood, but the idiomatic pronoun is missing. With a referent, it's ne vale la pena.
interference.it_to_es: Italians dropping ne land on exactly the right Spanish.
